title: New patient, dizziness on standing, diabetes and blood pressure

turns.text: Good morning, Mrs. Park. I'm Dr. Patel. What brings you in today?
I've been getting dizzy when I stand up, and I need a refill on my metformin.
When did the dizziness start?
About three days ago.
Any pain today, zero to ten?
No pain. Zero.
Your blood pressure today is one twenty-eight over seventy-eight, and your pulse is eighty-eight.
Temperature is ninety-eight point one, and your oxygen is ninety-seven percent.
Okay.
The nurse got your weight as one sixty-eight, and your height as five four.
Do you have any allergies?
Penicillin. I break out in hives.
What are you taking right now?
Metformin, a thousand milligrams twice a day, and amlodipine, five milligrams in the morning. I stopped the atorvastatin last month because my legs ached.
Got it, so no statin right now. Any other conditions besides the diabetes and blood pressure?
High cholesterol. That's why I was on the statin.
Any surgeries in the past?
No surgeries.
Have you ever smoked?
Never.
Do you drink alcohol?
I don't drink.
How much do you exercise?
I walk the dog maybe twice a week.
Besides the dizziness, any fever, chest pain, shortness of breath, cough, headache, or nausea?
A little nauseous in the mornings. Nothing else.
When was your last flu shot?
Two weeks ago at the pharmacy, so late September.
Tell me more about the dizziness.
When I stand up fast, the room spins for a few seconds. It started a few days after I began the amlodipine.
Okay, let's check your blood pressure standing up too.

notes: Must stay empty: SURG1 and SURG1_YEAR (no surgeries; skipped), DRINKS_WK (does not drink; skipped). Traps: the stopped atorvastatin must not appear as a current medication; past history comes from the clinician and the patient; 'in the morning' is once a day; flu shot two weeks before an October visit is this season.
